accuracy.reason: All eight objectives are accurate: reusable copies and authority, hit/miss, application-owned keys, invalidation races, expiration/eviction, local/shared scope, miss load and measured selection. No freshness guarantee is asserted.

evidence.quote: Invalidation alone does not guarantee freshness.

mechanisms.reason: The stack explains avoided work, explicit refill, paused-reader stale refill, TTL versus pressure, process isolation and concurrent miss amplification. Learner reconstructs the causal paths rather than naming policies.

evidence.quote: Coalescing requests lets concurrent readers share one in-progress lookup.

coherence.reason: Prerequisites cover API reads, commits, concurrency and finite capacity; cards progress from a reused copy to maintenance and failure. Diagram hit/miss and old-price paths agree with prose; shared renderer/CSS inspected, not executed.

evidence.quote: A hit can still return outdated data.

decisions.reason: Objectives about keys, freshness, sharing, overload and fit become concrete choices: both key inputs, authoritative latest reads, shared invalidation, bounded fallback and rejection of single-use caching.

evidence.quote: If requests rarely reuse results, or freshness is too hard to maintain, the cache may cost more than it saves.

clarity.reason: Short labeled mechanisms and a continuing price example distinguish presence, freshness and authority. TTL, eviction, coalescing and hit ratio are explained at first use; diagram does not imply automatic source synchronization.

evidence.quote: TTL limits an entry's lifetime, not the age of the source data used to fill it.

outcomes.reason: All criteria: keys station plus language; traces hit and explicit miss read/fill/return; compares 2ms hit with 80ms source work while retaining unspecified fill cost; identifies storage/upkeep and authoritative database.
All criteria: C receives old hours; delayed old read refills after deletion; rejects deletion as freshness guarantee; chooses direct authoritative reads under the stated commit visibility assumption.
All criteria: 12:03 can hit old weather, 12:11 misses, pressure eviction makes 12:05 miss; expiration and eviction remove usable copies without refreshing source data.

All criteria: local invalidation leaves three stale copies; chooses shared cache for shared deletion with stated network cost; contrasts local restart and common cache outage; rejects automatic database freshness.

All criteria: simultaneous misses repeat database work; coalesces pending same-key fetches; 10000 exceeds 500 by 20x; caps total fallback and rejects excess, only conditionally uses available permissible stale data; tests empty and unavailable cache.

All criteria: declines cache for one-use keys, 2ms reads within 100ms budget and 10/s within 1000/s capacity; names copy/lookup/upkeep costs; gives repeated expensive reads or load as triggers and measures benefits with staleness limits.

sourceChecks.claim: Azure caching guidance supports avoiding repeated source work and copy-management costs; database authority is explicitly scoped to this lesson.
Azure cache-aside specifies application lookup, source read and cache fill on miss, and warns cached data may diverge.
Azure caching guidance discusses keys and isolation; examples are application-derived identities, correctly including response-varying inputs.
Azure cache-aside supports source-write then invalidate and absence of guaranteed consistency; paused old-fill interleaving is valid reasoning from separate operations.
Redis eviction documents LRU, memory pressure and noeviction errors; Redis EXPIRE primary command reference confirms expiration removes a key rather than refreshing data.
AWS caching article compares per-process caches and external shared services, network/operating costs, coherence and shared dependency failure.
AWS article explicitly describes same-key herd, request coalescing, downstream overload, load shedding and cold-cache testing.
Azure guidance supports reuse, update/staleness policy, hit metrics and cost-benefit measurement; scenario selection is bounded by workload assumptions.
